submission.natural_language_explanation: Layer-0 grapheme detector for the letter h in the token currently being read: the pole fires on any token whose surface string starts with h/H, whether it is a bare or short piece or a hyphen/space/punctuation-prefixed one ('-H' 4.02, '-h' 3.91, 'HP' 3.63, 'H' 3.53, ' H' 3.48, 'h' 2.52, 'hl' 3.12, ' Harvard' 2.26) or the word-initial h that BPE leaves inside a longer word ('historic' 1.60 in 'prehistoric', 'hood' 0.93 in 'boyhood'), reaching 1.1-4.4 of the 4.4 scan max for all but its ~9% most frequent h-words (' have' 0.24, ' his' 0.19, ' here' 0.30, ' how' 0.12, ' however' 0.03), while tokens whose h is not leading stay at the floor (medians 0.11 for h-after-one-letter pieces like ' sh', 'ch', 0.00-0.01 for ' the', 'this', 'which', and 0.000 for tokens with no h at all), with only a weak residual band when h ends a short piece (' unh' 1.5, ' pH' 1.35, 'oh' 0.53). It is retrospective and context-invariant (token identity explains 99.7% of variance, position 0%, 91% of the input attribution on the peak token, and the same token gives the same strength in any sentence), orthographic rather than lexical (the invented word 'hox' fires at 3.17 against 'glorx' 0.06), and zero-ablating it costs the model the continuation of the h-word just read ('oo' after 'Boo-H', 'od' after 'non-H', 'ick' after 'oak-h') rather than any fixed upcoming token, so it is not lookahead.
